subject: Critical Thinking
title: The Semmelweis Reflex: Rejecting New Evidence
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Semmelweis Reflex: Rejecting New Evidence.

hook.text: Ignaz Semmelweis proved that handwashing prevented death in hospitals.

buildup.text: The Semmelweis reflex: automatically rejecting new information that contradicts established norms, beliefs, or.

discovery.text: Semmelweis reduced maternal deaths from 18% to 1% – & was fired, committed to an asylum, & beaten to death by guards.

twist.text: The same reflex appears whenever evidence threatens status, identity, or habit.

climax.text: Max Planck: 'Science advances one funeral at a time.' Sometimes the old guard must literally die before new truth is.

punchline.text: New evidence threatens old identities. That's why truth needs courage.

quiz.question: What is the Semmelweis reflex?
options: Automatically rejecting evidence that contradicts established beliefs

details.summary: The Semmelweis reflex is the automatic tendency to reject new evidence or knowledge that contradicts established norms or beliefs. Named after the doctor whose handwashing discovery was rejected by the medical establishment.
details.whyItMatters: This reflex has delayed scientific progress repeatedly and continues to cause resistance to paradigm shifts in medicine, science, and business.
takeaways: New evidence that contradicts established belief faces automatic resistance
The higher the status of existing beliefs, the stronger the rejection
Institutional culture can amplify or mitigate the reflex

faq.question: What happened to Ignaz Semmelweis when he proposed handwashing?
faq.answer: He demonstrated that handwashing dramatically reduced maternal death rates, but the medical establishment rejected his findings because they contradicted prevailing theory, and he died in disgrace.

faq.question: How does the Semmelweis reflex manifest in modern institutions?
faq.answer: Organizations resist process changes and new technologies that challenge existing expertise and power structures, even when evidence strongly supports the innovation.
